rules.source: Swedish Data Protection Act (Lag 2018:218) — lowers the GDPR Article 8 default age of consent for children's information-society-service data processing to 13 (vs. the GDPR default of 16), meaning a 13-year-old in Sweden can validly consent without a parent/guardian. https://www.imy.se/globalassets/dokument/rapporter/the-rights-of-children-and-young-people-on-digital-platforms_accessible.pdf

Swedish Data Protection Act (Lag 2018:218) — supplements GDPR with specific rules restricting processing of Swedish personal identity numbers (personnummer) to cases where clearly justified, and rules on processing data relating to criminal convictions/offences. https://pacmap.dev/regulation/se-data-protection-act-2018
Brottsbalken (Criminal Code) 4 kap. 9 c § (dataintrång) — Council of Europe Octopus Sweden profile https://www.coe.int/en/web/octopus/-/sweden
rules.retrieved_snippet: Council of Europe: most substantive Budapest Convention offences (illegal access, system and data interference, interception, misuse of devices) are currently interpreted through the provision on breach of data secrecy in Chapter 4, Section 9 c; university course material describes it as covering unauthorised access to or alteration of data for automated processing, with a fine or up to two years' imprisonment, and a grave form (grovt dataintrång) added in 2014. Profile may be out of date.

rules.source: Brottsbalken 16 kap. 8 § (hets mot folkgrupp) — Riksdag committee report https://www.riksdagen.se/sv/dokument-och-lagar/dokument/betankande/om-hets-mot-folkgrupp-m-m-prop-19818258_g501juu41/html/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Summaries: the offence covers threatening or expressing contempt for a population group in a message that is spread, on grounds of race, skin colour, national or ethnic origin, religious belief and (since 2003) sexual orientation, with up to two years' imprisonment (grave cases six months to four years); a February 2024 referral proposed clarifying the provision, enactment not confirmed.

rules.source: Spellagen (2018:1138) and Marknadsföringslagen (2008:486) — Swedish Gambling Authority / Consumer Agency guidance via https://regulations.clym.io/swedens-gambling-act-2018-1138
rules.retrieved_snippet: Secondary summaries: the Gambling Act took effect 1 January 2019, ended the state monopoly and introduced a licensing system supervised by Spelinspektionen; Chapter 15 Section 1 sets a moderation requirement for gambling marketing and marketing may not be directed at children and young people; the Consumer Agency adopted general advice on game marketing on 15 January 2025 covering both laws. Not an official source.
